Upon my asking if arranging a demo even if it is at a later date would be possible he said that it wasn't and repeated that the reason was the high demand. After this he began pushing support pages onto me as an alternative. ### Slow Loading Times and Performance Issues

Documents take 30+ seconds to open for recipients. Preview images won't generate. Page navigation within documents becomes sluggish. Recipients complain about frustrating user experience.

Server overload or Content Delivery Network (CDN) problems cause these symptoms. When DocSend's infrastructure struggles, document delivery suffers even if core systems remain technically "operational." Poor performance drives recipients away before viewing critical content.

### Access Permission and Security Errors [...] ### Social Media Monitoring

Search Twitter/X for @DocSend or #docsenddown to find real-time user complaints. Social media reports often appear faster than official status updates, especially during rapidly developing outages. Look for multiple users reporting identical issues from different locations.

### Common Error Messages Indicating DocSend Outages

When DocSend experiences problems, you'll typically see these error messages:

"Service Unavailable" or "503 Error" - Indicates server overload or maintenance. Backend systems can't handle current request volume.

"502 Bad Gateway" - Backend server communication failure. The DocSend application servers aren't responding to load balancer requests. [...] These issues intensify during peak business hours (9-11 AM PST, 1-3 PM EST), suggesting server capacity problems. The upload infrastructure struggles to handle concurrent upload volumes, leading to failures and timeouts.

Common upload error patterns:

 PDFs under 10MB upload successfully, larger files fail
 Uploads work in early morning/late evening, fail during business hours
 Upload appears to complete but document isn't accessible
 Repeated "Network error" or "Connection timeout" messages

### Link Generation Broken or Failing

Documents upload successfully, but clicking "Create Link" or "Share" produces no result. Buttons become unresponsive. Generated links return 404 errors when recipients try accessing them. Previously working links suddenly break.

results.title: AI Agents for M&A Q&A: Secure Data Room Due Diligence with MCP | DocSend
results.content:
### The core risks

 Data exfiltration. If the AI agent sends data room content to an external model or API, that data has left your controlled environment. In a deal context, that's potentially catastrophic.
 Overexposure. A bidder group's AI agent shouldn't see documents restricted to another bidder group. Permissions that exist in the VDR must carry through to the AI layer.
 Model training exposure. If the AI provider trains on your inputs, your confidential deal data could surface in someone else's query response.
 No deal-specific access controls. Generic AI tools don't understand deal structures: bidder groups, confidentiality tiers, document-level permissions, or clean-team boundaries.

### Why traditional AI integration falls short [...] Configure the AI agent's Q&A workflow:

1. Intake: The agent receives a question from the VDR's Q&A module (via MCP)
2. Retrieval: The agent searches the data room through MCP for relevant documents, scoped to the correct bidder-group permissions.
3. Drafting: The agent reads the relevant documents and drafts a structured answer with source citations.
4. Review & approval: The human reviewer edits, approves, or rejects the draft.
5. Posting: The approved answer is posted to the VDR Q&A module with supporting document references.

### Step 5: Establish human checkpoints

AI-assisted doesn't mean AI-autonomous.
